headline: A preprint reports gains from adapting agent skills to executor capability
summary: A 24-page arXiv preprint reports that reusable agent skills can help stronger models while providing little benefit or even reducing scores for weaker executors. Across 607 tasks in SkillsBench, DocOps and Tessl, the authors selected 103 skill-sensitive task-skill pairs and mapped failures to tool execution, context management, instruction following and verification. A fixed meta-skill used to adapt skill wording improved three weak executors in one-shot tests when applied by stronger rewriters; in a five-round self-evolution experiment, the meta-skill arm finished above the no-meta arm for all seven executors. These are author-reported benchmark results, not independently reproduced outcomes; each model-task-condition cell was run once in the described experiments. The authors’ project page now links a public reproduction repository with task indexes and experiment code, but this activation did not pin or run it.
